claims.explanation: Idarubicin kills via topoisomerase II (TOP2A) poisoning, so selectivity is likely driven by proliferative/TOP2A-dependent biology and by intact DNA-damage/apoptosis signaling. Sensitive lines are enriched for MAPK-pathway activation (BRAF/NRAS/MAP2K1) and PIK3CA/PTEN alterations, which increase proliferation and TOP2A dependence, while resistant lines often carry RB1 loss or are slow-growing sarcoma/mesothelioma lines. TP53 mutation is nearly universal and therefore not discriminating; features such as BRAF/NRAS mutation, PIK3CA mutation, and EGFR mutation are candidate sensitizers, whereas RB1 loss and low TOP2A expression are candidate protectors.

PIK3CA-mutant gastric/colorectal/ovarian lines are enriched in the sensitive set; PI3K activation supports proliferation
PTEN loss in melanoma/breast/endometrial sensitive lines; PI3K pathway activation
EGFR-mutant NSCLC and esophageal lines appear in the sensitive set; oncogene-driven proliferation
Idarubicin targets TOP2A; higher TOP2A expression increases drug-induced DNA damage
RB1-mutant gastric/ovarian lines are in the resistant set; RB loss may reduce proliferation/drug sensitivity
ATM-mutant lines appear in the resistant set; impaired DNA-damage response may reduce anthracycline efficacy
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not a strong discriminator; listed only as a weak/negative feature
FLT3-ITD AML is treated with anthracyclines including idarubicin, suggesting FLT3-driven leukemias are sensitive
CEBPA mutations are favorable prognostic markers in AML treated with anthracycline-based regimens
